provenance.paper_title: Authoring for Living Worlds: Tool-Constrained LLM Agents for Executable Multi-Actor Scenarios

representation_paths.memory_component: Persistent simulated world state via the event graph (entities/state across events)

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: Executable event-graph nodes; World state. The same entities and state are carried across events in the simulated world.

During operation, GEST applies fixed-rule insertion or replacement to Persistent simulated world state via the event graph (entities/state across events); the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

During operation, GEST applies fixed-rule correction of stored state to Persistent simulated world state via the event graph (entities/state across events); the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

During operation, GEST applies relinking or reindexing of stored items to Persistent simulated world state via the event graph (entities/state across events); the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 6): During inference, the operative memory component (Persistent simulated world state via the event graph (entities/state across events)) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, fixed-rule correction of stored state, relinking or reindexing of stored items; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
